chapter: Uptown clubs and the Black Cat
title: Luckey Roberts and records with James P.
summary: Greene never heard Luckey Roberts, and mentions making records with James P. Johnson and Pee Wee Russell.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: What I was really wondering was -- about him -- not having heard him. Would you say he was more like Luckey Roberts than Fats Waller, say ?.
Well, I never had a chance, really, to hear Roberts.
Oh.
Do you see what I mean? I never heard him. I heard Willie talk about him.
Yeah.
And everybody else, you know used to talk about Luckey Roberts.
Yeah.
I often wondered, who's Lucky Roberts? Luckey Roberts had all the best jobs.
They say, -- they used to tell me he had all the best jobs.
But, you didn't really get to hear him?
No.
Well, he used to come over and play for millionaires at the Louisville club...
Yes. Yes. Yes.
...they'd ship him to Chicago.
How would you contrast him with Fats, for instance? With Fats Waller. Would he be a little back of him for, like, generation, or --
Hm. I don't know how to classify him.
Yeah.
I mean, as far as Fats.
Yeah. Yeah. He's a little difficult to. What about
like James P.
Well, of course, James P. really played more blues than --
No, he's kind of versatile.
Yeah.
I made a couple records -- one record with him -- or a couple I guess with James P.
Did you know that? That Freddie made some records with James P.
No.
We made -- I made a thing with him and Pee Wee Russell.
Oh, yes, yes. I remember those.
Do you remember that?
Yeah. Wasn't that for Steve Smith's label?
I don't know. I don't remember.
